role: Brand director B — recognition, distinctive behavior, and Nag attribution
observedStrengths: The unequal paddle antennae, oversized cream head, tiny feet, and green marked wings form a coherent visual vocabulary. The identity sheet preserves these cues across themes; the native SVG and character source keep geometry separate from palette.

The header pairs the moth directly with a large, readable heyNag wordmark. The 390px README evidence follows it immediately with first-person software work, so the current application attributes the character to Nag rather than leaving it as an unexplained mascot.
Question-led project introductions support curiosity with named, concrete work. The story's notice–get into it–share pattern can persist beyond any current software platform.
The poses remain innocent and approachable even when skeptical or frustrated. This restraint leaves room for wry behavior without abandoning the chosen character.

concreteConcerns.claim: The default public expression establishes warmth more strongly than Nag's wry, mischievous side.
concreteConcerns.evidence: identity.png and readme-390-day.png show the same open smile and raised mitten in the header. all-24.png contains mischievous and skeptical acting, but those signals are not part of the current principal identity application. This is a personality-weighting concern, not a request for a new website.

concreteConcerns.claim: The avatar depends heavily on antenna asymmetry for distinctiveness; its crop removes the wings that most clearly communicate moth.
concreteConcerns.evidence: identity.png's 32–160px avatar row retains the head and two paddles but no wing marks. At the smallest displayed sizes the details compress into a friendly cream face with green tips. This is a perceptual risk worth testing, not evidence that viewers confuse it.

concreteConcerns.claim: The emotional library is broader than the currently demonstrated brand behavior.
concreteConcerns.evidence: all-24.png presents many moods at equal visual priority, while story.md specifies a repeatable notice–get into it–share rhythm. A catalogue alone does not yet demonstrate which tiny gesture or timing pattern should repeatedly mean heyNag. The current foundation needs a signature selection, not more emotions.

qualityCriteriaForNine: Preserve the tiny V5 proportions, four marked wings, unequal paddles, and identical geometry/poses across themes.
Select a small signature repertoire that makes curious, geeky, and gently mischievous feel like one personality; retain other states as supporting vocabulary.
Demonstrate one silent, finite signature performance and its canonical still at actual application sizes, with legible intent in both themes.
Maintain immediate heyNag/Nag attribution wherever the mascot is introduced, and keep first-person project evidence stronger than decorative storytelling.
Record expert appeal judgments separately from any later unaided recognition, attribution, and delayed-recall observations; do not award research certainty through panel agreement.
highestValueExperiment: Within the existing motion studio, compare three short treatments of the same honest project question: the current curious baseline; notice → geeky investigation → warm share; and the same sequence with one restrained wry hesitation. Use existing anatomy and props, identical duration and framing, silent playback, and the same heyNag author line. Review the canonical still plus 96px and 160px playback in both themes. Select for clear thought, warmth, and personality rather than quantity of movement. A later human test should separately check whether viewers connect the character to Nag after a delay.
limits: Independently reviewed README.md, story.md, current SVG/source assets, and all four requested evidence images before reading any other reviewer.
Still evidence and source inspection support visual and brand-system judgments; I did not view live temporal playback.
No human recognition, attribution, attachment, or recall data is available. Website/scenery absence and the silent baseline are not defects.
